obligation: Corporate (subcontractor) notice to BDS
citation: 45 CFR 164.410 (a subcontractor is a business associate of the business associate, 160.103); intercompany BAA (2023)
trigger: Corporate, which operates the legacy cloud account for the DPCP, discovers a breach of unsecured PHI it holds for BDS
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery (shorter if the BAA says so)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CAD and file transfer servers
clock_starts: Discovery by any corporate employee or agent (164.410(a)(2))

obligation: BDS (business associate) notice to Ambulance Services
trigger: Breach of unsecured Ambulance Services PHI in the CAD database or claim files
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; intercompany BAA sets 5 business days
clock_starts: Discovery by any BDS employee or agent; this runbook uses the day the SOC knew

obligation: BDS (business associate) notice to Urgent Care
trigger: Breach of unsecured Urgent Care PHI in claim files on the file transfer servers
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; intercompany BAA sets 5 business days

obligation: Content of business associate notices
trigger: Every business associate breach notice
deadline: With the notice: identification of each individual affected, to the extent possible, and other information the covered entity needs for its own notice, as it becomes available

obligation: Ambulance Services breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows a low probability of compromise)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected individual (first-class mail; substitute notice if contact information is out of date for 10 or more)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any workforce member or agent (164.404(a)(2))

obligation: Ambulance Services notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice (within 60 days of discovery)
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes (millions of records in this scenario)

obligation: Ambulance Services media notice
trigger: More than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction affected
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets in each such state
notifying_entity: Ambulance Services Privacy Officer with group communications

obligation: Urgent Care breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of unsecured Urgent Care PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - separate covered entity (no affiliated covered entity designation)

obligation: Urgent Care notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal

obligation: Urgent Care media notice
trigger: More than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction affected
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets in each such state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the state count exceeds 500

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
trigger: A covered entity breach affects fewer than 500 individuals
deadline: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a later, separate breach is under 500

obligation: Law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement official states that notice would impede an investigation
deadline: Delay for the period stated in writing; up to 30 days if the statement is oral and documented

obligation: BDS notice to affected dispatch client agencies
trigger: Breach of a client agency's PHI in its CAD partition (9 of 14 clients in this scenario)
deadline: Per each BAA and never later than 60 calendar days after discovery

obligation: BDS notice to affected billing clients
trigger: Breach of a billing client's PHI in claim files (23 clients in this scenario)
deadline: 72 hours after discovery for the 31 clients with negotiated terms; 10 calendar days under the standard BAA; never later than 60 days

obligation: BDS security incident report to other clients
trigger: Security incident affecting the service without a breach of that client's PHI
deadline: Standard BAA: 5 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for unaffected dispatch and billing clients

obligation: Client covered entities' own notices
trigger: Clients decide their own breach notices after BDS notice
deadline: Per HIPAA, from the client's own discovery date

obligation: Client dispatch contract outage notice
trigger: CAD outage or manual dispatch at any center serving the client
deadline: Phone call to the client duty officer within 15 minutes; written report within 24 hours

obligation: County ambulance agreement notices
citation: 38 county and municipal ambulance agreements (contract, not law)
trigger: Dispatch disruption affecting a county or municipal zone
deadline: Immediate phone call to the county PSAP supervisor; written report within the period each agreement sets (most say 24 hours)
notify: County PSAP supervisors; county EMS contract managers

obligation: State breach notification laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents
deadline: Varies by state (for example "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days)
notify: Residents; state attorneys general or regulators where required; consumer reporting agencies above state thresholds
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside
notifying_entity: Each covered entity with counsel; BDS for clients where it is the third-party agent

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of personal information (includes medical and health insurance information) of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15 more days only if good cause is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within the 30 days, 501.171(3)(a)); notice under HIPAA is deemed compliant if a copy is timely provided to the Department
notifying_entity: Ambulance Services and Urgent Care Privacy Officers

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (no extension for this notice)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice (worked example)
trigger: A third-party agent maintaining personal information for a covered entity discovers a breach
deadline: No later than 10 days after determination
notify: The covered entity (internal divisions and Florida clients)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - BDS and corporate act as third-party agents

obligation: State EMS licensing office notice
citation: State EMS license conditions (not verified in this sample)
trigger: Loss of dispatch capability or a breach of patient care records
deadline: Confirm with each state EMS office before use
notify: State EMS offices in the 7 states

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the annual report

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As soon as practicable
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (voluntary until then). If finalized as proposed, Ambulance Services would be covered (EMS to a population of 50,000 or more, proposed 226.2(b)(5)). Recheck when final

obligation: CJIS incident reporting (IR-6)
trigger: Incident involving criminal justice information
deadline: Personnel report suspected incidents to the organization's incident response capability immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: Organizational incident handlers, and the CSO, SIB Chief or Interface Agency Official, and the FBI CJIS ISO
applies_at_this_tier: Conditional - only if the county's CJIS Systems Agency determines the premise notes still held in the CAD database are CJI (P03 BD-G28). Tell the county at once in any case

obligation: Card brand and acquirer notice
citation: Merchant agreement and card brand rules (contract; PCI DSS Requirement 12.10 topic)
trigger: Suspected compromise of card data
deadline: Per the acquirer agreement
applies_at_this_tier: No in this scenario (the contact-center service was not affected); keep in the matrix

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (as soon as practicable; use the carrier hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: Covered telecommunications / Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts (Medicare and Medicaid billing is not a procurement contract)

obligation: Part 2 and FTC Health Breach Notification Rule
trigger: Breach of Part 2 records or of a non-HIPAA personal health record
deadline: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No - no Part 2 program; all divisions are covered entities or business associates
